new_statements.quote: Aquí hay que señalar que en todas las lenguas arus el acento de la palabra incide automáticamente en su penúltima sílaba. Sin embargo, en cauqui, a juzgar por los datos de que disponemos, pareciera haberse desarrollado un rasgo de intensidad vocálica que se efectiviza únicamente en la penúltima y la antepenúltima sílabas de las raíces: si la vocal intensa ocurre en la antepenúltima sílaba, se lleva toda o casi toda la carga acentual hacia su sílaba; si ocurre en la penúltima sílaba, se realiza como vocal larga acentuada.
new_statements.translation: It should be pointed out here that in all the Aru languages word accent falls automatically on the penultimate syllable. However, in Cauqui, judging from the data available to us, a feature of vowel intensity seems to have developed which is realised only in the penultimate and antepenultimate syllables of roots: if the intense vowel occurs in the antepenultimate syllable, it draws all or almost all of the accentual load onto its syllable; if it occurs in the penultimate syllable, it is realised as a long stressed vowel.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is automatic (non-contrastive) on the penultimate syllable/vowel, as throughout Aymaran; Hardman's own family description, as relayed by Martín (1984/85: 'en las tres lenguas [aymara, jaqaru, kawki] el acento recae en la penúltima vocal') says the same explicitly for Kawki, and Hardman's Alfabeto (1998) states Kawki has 'la misma estructura' as Jaqaru, for which she gives 'el acento no es fonémico; ocurre en la vocal penúltima' (1963: 237) and 'Word stress is penultimate for all...' (2000: 5). Position is counted in vowels (Hardman) because of heavy clusters/vowel dropping.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing Kawki-specific. For Jaqaru: Hardman 1966 — in words of three or more vowels a secondary stress occurs before the main stress; Hardman 2000: 52 — reduplicatives sometimes keep a secondary stress on the first member where its stress would have been; Cerrón-Palomino 1994 — many trisyllables show initial secondary prominence with vowel lengthening ([a:páka]).
new_statements.exceptions: Torero: in 'cauqui' roots an 'intense' (long) vowel in the antepenult attracts the stress (antepenultimate stress); in the penult it surfaces as a long stressed vowel. Cerrón-Palomino 1994 (Tupe Jaqaru): loans ending in a consonant keep their original stress after vowel paragoge (shúqushu, háwasha); some suffixes (agentive -iri, participial -ta) do not shift stress (ál-k-iri). Hardman 2000: 52: stress stays on the penultimate (underlying) vowel 'whether the final vowel is dropped or not'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('acento de la palabra'; Hardman: penultimate vowel of the phonological word, falling pitch marks word end; intonation 'fonológicamente irrelevante'). Statements are impressionistic; no instrumental work on Kawki found.
new_statements.identity_note: cauq1239 = Kawki ('cauqui') of Cachuy, Chavín de Yauyos and Canchán (Hardman 1975: 433; 20-30 speakers then), split from Jaqaru of Tupe/Aiza/Colca (jaqa1244) by Glottolog on Hardman 1978:148. Naming is treacherous: (i) Torero (1970, 2002) uses 'cauqui' for the whole surviving Yauyos Aru language ('cauqui de Tupe y cauqui de Cachuy', which he holds to be 'una sola lengua'), so the quoted statement covers Cachuy Kawki but is not specific to it; (ii) Farfán 1952 and Matos Mar 1956 use 'kawki/kauke/haqe-aru' for the Tupe language as well; (iii) Cerrón-Palomino (2000 BFUCh fn.) restricts 'cauqui' to the hablas of Cachuy and Catahuasi and treats them as a dialect of 'aimara central/tupino'; (iv) Hardman treats Kawki as a separate sister language but says its structure/alphabet is the same as Jaqaru's. The only first-hand, full-text accent statement obtained (Hardman 1963 RMN 32: 237, 'En jaqaru el acento no es fonémico. Ocurre en la vocal penúltima') is for Tupe Jaqaru (jaqa1244), saved in this folder and usable for that entry.

sources.note: §6 'Interludio prosódico' (pp. 77-78): Jaqaru (Tupe) accent regime is 'básicamente llano o grave' (penultimate); many trisyllables carry a secondary initial prominence with lengthening ([a:páka]); accent is sensitive to underlying form and morphology (loans keep original penult stress after paragoge, e.g. shúqushu; agentive -iri does not count: ál-k-iri). Tupe data only; no Cachuy statement.

sources.note: Second-hand summary of Hardman's Jaqi family description (Hardman 1978): "Las lenguas jaqi tienen tres vocales fonémicas, i, u, a... pero donde aymara y kawki tienen i, jaqaru tiene u. La palabra se inicia con el alófono vocálico más alto y en las tres lenguas [aymara, jaqaru, kawki] el acento recae en la penúltima vocal. La entonación es fonológicamente irrelevante, siendo un recurso de estilo." Also: kawki and jaqaru lack phonemic long vowels.

sources.note: Snippet: "STRESS Stress in Jaqaru is non-phonemic. It normally occurs on the penultimate vowel of the word and is frequently accompanied by a rise in pitch. The normal pattern for a two vowel word is: káĉa 'manta'. In words of three vowels or more, a secondary stress occurs before the main stress." Jaqaru of Tupe; Kawki not separately treated.
